findings.title: should_block? side effects run on every validation, double-counting matches on signup
findings.body: `should_block?` increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and saves the record every time it is called. It is called from `EmailValidator`, which runs on every `valid?`/`save`. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (when `call_discourse_hub?` is on) and then `user.save`, so one signup attempt bumps the counter twice. Any other code path that validates repeatedly inflates the statistics the same way. Validation should be a pure check; record the match once, explicitly, at the point of rejection.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1; record.save` loads the value, increments it in Ruby and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked address can lose increments. Use an atomic SQL update instead, e.g. `update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or `increment_counter`.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and easily bypassed
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact, case-sensitive match. The unique index and uniqueness validation are also case-sensitive. Email addresses are effectively case-insensitive, so a blocked `bad@spam.org` can register as `Bad@Spam.org`. Normalize the address (e.g. `Email.downcase`) on both storage and lookup, or compare with `lower(email)`.

findings.title: Rejected email compared against server-returned value, which may differ from the typed input
findings.body: The client stores `result.values.email`, the server-side model attribute, in `rejectedEmails`. It then checks `rejectedEmails.contains(accountEmail)` against the raw input. If the server normalizes the email (case, whitespace), the stored value will not equal what the user typed. The field will then not be marked invalid, and the user can resubmit the same rejected address. Store the locally submitted `email` instead.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array defined on prototype is shared across instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` inside `extend` creates one array on the class prototype. Every instance of `CreateAccountController` mutates the same array via `pushObject`. Rejected emails therefore persist across modal openings and instances. Initialize it in `init` instead.
